touches.text: Install and upgrades live here: the installer machine walks the host-seam intentions, verifies each, offers what's missing, applies, re-verifies. If xyz library needs an update, this is the component that does it. Any change to what the host is goes through here (6.6.3.1.1).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal. Akien 2026-11-13, answering Q#90 (a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal, measured 2026-11-12): "then we have to invent a way for seals to be host independent. one way would be to create a sealing machine in cairn. there's only ever one cairn until we have a laptop die and have to fail over to a backup".
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

Scripts are Python wherever possible, run by Cairn's own interpreter, so one file works on every platform. Platform-specific ones match their platform: executable or .sh on Linux; .bat, .cmd or .ps1 on Windows.
